context: Icicle partition chart of a synthetic 500-file filesystem hierarchy, linked to a brushable log-scale histogram for filtering by file size.
first_impression: Structurally honest visualization with correct partition area encoding, data-driven domains, and proper log-scale handling for skewed file-size data.
what_works: Histogram Y-axis correctly starts at 0 with data-driven domain (d3.max); log-spaced bin thresholds are appropriate for the log-normal size distribution; icicle uses getPath(d) as key function for object constancy; brush inversion correctly uses histX.invert() on the log scale.
what_doesnt: Histogram uses a hardcoded 30-bin count rather than a data-driven rule (Sturges/Scott), though log-spaced bins are a reasonable choice; xMin is computed as d3.min(sizes)*0.8 which could theoretically approach zero on very small files, risking log-scale breakage.
